answer: Random-walk trust scoring stops Sybils by treating the social graph like a meadow crossed by footpaths: short random walks from known honest agents almost never wander into a fake cluster, because the two regions share only a handful of attack edges. A whisper of trust travels along real relationships, so a Sybil pocket stays isolated even as it grows dense inside. Like juniper roots that only spread where the soil is real, each fake identity needs genuine links to honest users to earn any score — and forging thousands of those by hand costs far more than the rewards are worth.
